SPECIFICATION FOR COMMERCIAL COOKING RANGES INCLUDING GRILLERS FOR USE WITH LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GASES 0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 20 October 1976, after the draft finalized by the Domestic and Commerce.! Gas Burning Appliances (Pressure Type) Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consumer Products and Medical Instruments Division Council.
0.2 In preparing this standard assistance has been derived from ANSI Z 21.3-1973 `Specification for hotel and restaurant gas ranges and unit broilers', issued by the American National Standards Institute. 0.3 This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards on various domestic and commercial gas burning appliances (pressure type) used with Liquefied IS : 5 116-1969* is a necessary adjunct to this Petroleum Gases (LPG). Should, howcvcr, any deviation exist between the requirements standard. given in IS : 5 11 G-1969* and those of this standard, provisions of the latter shall apply.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard specifies construction, operation, safety requirements and tests for commercial cooking ranges including grillers having a total gas consumption of more than 1 500 g/h, intended for use with Liquefied Petroleum Gases at 2.9 kN/m2t gas inlet pressure.

3.1 The construction of all parts, whether specifically covered by the various sections of this standard or not, shall be in accordance with the reasonable concepts of safety, substantiality and durability. 3.2 The general ccnstruction and assembly shall be neat with parts wellfitted and bolts and other fasteners drawn up tightly to give rigidity. Exposed edges shall be rounded off and all adjustments shall be accessible and easy to operate. 3.3 No pressure regulator shall be included as a part of the cooking range.

5.6 The use of oven and broiler burners in one oven shall not be permitted unless the control of these burners is such that they cannot be operated at the same time. 5.7 Electrical components requiring field adjustment or calibrations shall be readily accessible when the appliance is installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. If operation of the appliance is necessary, to make such adjustments, means for making the adjustment shall be possible without exposing electrical live parts, disturbing wiring and without the necessity of manipulating tools with any burner compartment. 5.8 By direct or indirect means it shall be possible to ascertain whether each electrically controlled component is functioning with the appliance installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions without disassembly of the appliance to a degree which would render it inoperative. 5.9 Means shall be provided for changing fuses and lamps with the appliance installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions without exposing electrically live parts except screws, shells or clips of lampholders and fuseholders. 9.0 In addition to the relevant requirements of burners specified in Section of IS : 5116-1969*, the requirements given in 9.1 to 9.20 shall apply. 9.1 Main positioned burners and mixers tubes shail be properly placed and securely so that the burners will not twist or slide or drop out of position

The construction shall be such that the burners cannot be installed in other than their correct position_ 9.2 The design and material used in the construction of burners and their support shall be such that neither the burner nor its support will sag, distort, melt, exhibit appreciable corrosion or damage to any protective coating sufficient to expose the base metal or show leakage of gas during any of the tests specified therein or when the burner is operating and the flame burning within the mixer tube or burner brad. 9.3 Main burners and pilot device or any assembly thereof shall be easily removable and replaceable through the excess openin@ without disconnecting threaded joints other than those of a union type. Simple disconnection such as the removing of a readily accessible manifold pipe by disconnecting a union shall be permitted if the appliance is equipped with a manual main control valve located on the inlet side of such a connection. Disconnection, removal and reassembly shall be accomplished without the use of special tools or requiring tool manipulation within the burner compartment. 9.4 The joints when used in the burner zone or in the burner head of the burner assembly, shall be gas tight and shall not depend for mechanical strength, primarily far tightness of' set screws, cement or other ceiling materials except where such joints form part of the port area. The burners head shall be of single casting or the joints shall be welded, brazed, bolted screwy joint construction or of any equally rigid and gas type construction. 9.5 Burners which are made of two or more parts shall have joints betlveen parts made tightly and permanentI>-. a.nd the burners shall be easily removable ah tine piece. 9.6 Ribbon burners shall be constructed so that the ribbon assembly can be easily removed thoroughly cleaned and easily and correctly reinstalled in the field without the use of the special tools. 9.7 When air shutters smoothly finislied. 9.8 When are used, burner mixer heads shall have flat faces

10. BURNER

SUPPORTS

10.1 Top burner supports shall be such that they will keep the burner(s) fixed rigidly at a uniform distance below the cooking surface. Rurner supports shall also secure the burner(s) against side-to-side and front-to-back displacement and prevent the burner(s) from being easily dislodged.
10.2 Oven burner supports shall be of rigid construction and shall hold the burners so that they lie level and cannot be easily tilted. 10.3 The support shall not interfere with the burner ports. 1.12 mm and

10.4 Sheet-iron shall be bolted,

oven burner supports riveted or spot-welded

shall not be less than in place.

10.5 Ceramic radiants shall be supported so that they are positioned at a uniform distance from the burner and so that the ceramics will not be dislodged in service. 10.6 Supports for ceramic radiants durable and heat-resistant material. or welded. 11. PRIMARY shall be of rigid construction and of Cast-iron supports shall not be riveted

AIR CONTROL

11.1 When adjustable means are provided for control of primarv air to the main burner(s) they shall be constructed so as to permit adj'ustment of flames to yellow tips and to lifting, a hard flame or flashback. The range of adjustment of flames from yellow tips to lifting, hard flames or flashback shall be easily obtained and of reasonable magnitude.
11.2 When air shutters are used, there shall be no openings other than the Air adjustable openings through which primary air may be entrained. shutters shall be of such design that they have not more than two primary air openings each approximating a circular opening near point of closure or be of such design and construction as can be demonstrated to provide Other equally effective protection against stoppage by lint and dust. openings through which the main stream of primary air does not flow, such as around an orifice projection, shall be reduced to a practical minimum so as to have no appreciable effect on the flamecharacteristics when stopped by lint or other means. 11.3 Means shall be provided to fix air shutters securely in any desired Such means shall be conveniently accessible for atljustm?nt \yith position. 10

IS : 8251- 1976 thr lnmwm in place and in operation and shall be located so as not to interfere \I-it11adjustmrnt of orifice caps when used.
11.4 Sheet-metal air shutters shall be of a thickness not less than 0.80 mm. II` shrct-metal air shutters are of a thickness less than 1.25 mm, they shall ha\c the outer edges turned & right angles or bc otherwise properly reinforced. 11.5 Air shutters shall have a corrosion-resisting finish, except when the typt' of material or construction employed will prevent sticking or corroding Cast-iron air shutters are considered to be acceptable. in position. 11.6 Unit broilers shall have the mixer heads protected or located prevent contamination of the primary air supply by the broiler vapours. 12. BASES, LEGS AND FRAMES so as to cooking

12.1 Rand iron, angle iron or other structural shapes used in the construction of bases and frames shall have joints securely riveted or welded together or to the body sides. 12.2 Ca,st bases and frames, when not cast in one piece, shall have joints securely fastened to give effectively a one-piece construction. 12.3 Sheet iron used in the construction of bases and frames shall not be less than 1.25 mm, and edges shall be reinforced, as by folding. 12.4 Legs shall be rigidly held in place. levellers shall be provided on applian-

12.5 When legs are provided, suitable ces designed for battery installation.

12.6 Commercial ranges shall support, without breakage or apparent damage for a period of 15 minutes, a load of 3.6 kN* applied without impact across the ccntre of the two weakest members of the top of the range tested as given in 12.6.1. 12.6.1 The top grates or solid plates shall be removed. A wooden beam 150 mm square shall then be placed across the two weakest members of the top frame at their centres. A load of 3.6 kN shall then be applied without shock at the centre of the beam and the effect noted. 12.7 Legs up to 205 mm in height a.nd bases shall be substantial and rigid to the extent that they will not be deformed or damaged by moving the assembled range 0.9 m along a smooth concrete floor endwise or sidewise by pressure exerted in a normal manner against the top end or top side, respectively, suffirirnt to cause the range to move ficely.

13.0 Commercial cooking ranges shall be equipped with a pilot burner In addition to the requirements given in 12 and and safety shutoff device, 13 of IS : 5116-1969*, the requirements given in 13.1 to 13.12 shall also
apply* 13.1 Burners located in enclosed compartments, except top sections, shall be equipped with a pilot burner and safety shutoff device. 13.2 Pilot burner and safety shutoff device assemblies having input ratings in excess of 1 046 kJt per hour shall automatically shutoff the gas to ail burners, including pilot burners, in the event that the means of ignition become inoperative. 13.3 Pilot burner and safety shutoff device assemblies having input ratings of 1 046 kJ per hour or less need not be of the complete shutoff type. 13.4 Tips of aerated pilot burners shall be made from stainless Designation 3OCr13 of IS : 6603-19721 or material having at least lent heat and corrosion-resistant characteristics. Nickel alloys of than 1.0 percent nickel, because of catalytic cracking effect-, are not able. steel of equivagreater accepi-

13.5 Fixed primary air openings of blue flame pilot burners shall br of a size that will give a satisfactory flame when using the manufacturer's recommended orifice size for each of the test gases. 13.5.1 When air shutters are used, there shall be no openings other than Air the adjustable openings through which primary air may be entrained. shutters shall be of such design that they have not more than two primary air openings each approximating a circular opening near point of closure, or be of such design and construction as can be demonstrated to provide Air shutters equally effective protection against stoppage by lint and dust. shall have adequate means for holding them in the desired adjustment position. 13.6 Pilot burners shall be placed so that lighted, and readily removed for cleaning. they can be easily seen, safely

13.9 Pilot burners shall be designed and installed so that the relative position of the pilot and separate lighter arm(s), when employed, or main Mounting of the pilot, separate lighter burner(s) will remain constant. arm, or main burner directly or indirectly on members. that may warp in service with resultant misalignment between pilot, separate lighter arm, and main burner shall not be considered as complying with this provision. A single bolt and nut, tap bolt, or equivalent removable means used in attaching the pilot to the main burner, or to a separate lighter arm, in order to effect compliance with this provision shall not be considered as failure. 13.10 Provisions shall be made for an adequate supply of air at all rimes for combustion of the gases from the pilot burner. 13.11 When a separate pilot burner is used, the design of the control system shall be such that gas cannot be admitted to the main burner while the pilot burner is being lighted and until the safety shutoff device will remain in its normal open position. 13.12 The temperature of a safety shutoff device during conduct of the wall and floor temperature test shall not exceed a temperature of 13.5"C, below that temperature for which the device is designed. 14.

1976 AND BROILER LININGS

20.X Ovens and broilers shall be furnished \vith linings at t11c sides and hack which provide cithcr (a) air space insulation, or (1,) enclo~d solid insulation. 20.2 Linings of ovens and broilers shall be constructed resistant material or have a corrosion-resisting finish. 20.3 When linings arc used solely for air space insulation, be less than 12.5 mm non-circulating air space. 20.4 When the back space less than 19 mm space. is used for flue purposes, of a corrohionthere shall not shall not be

there

20.5 Ovens shall be furnished with a top lining. When the top space is used for flue purposes, it shall provide not less than a 19 mm space. 20.6 Linings, except for salamander broilers, shall be removable unless constructed of corrosion-resistant metal or possessing a corrosion-resistant coating, or constructed of sheet metal at least as thick as 1.60 mm. If lining is of the removable type, it shall be held in place without bolts. 20.6.1 No interference to easy removal of unbolted linings shall be offered by presence of accessories, such as oven heat regulators and oven pilots. The simple unscrewing of one or two unions, or bolts, shall not be construed as offering intcrfcrcnce, although it is urged that the construction be such that the linings may be rcmov?d without need of disconnecting the accessories. 20.6.2 Similarly, accessories of removing bolted linings. 20.7 Suitable should be easily detachable without the need

IS : 8251 - 1976 40. OVEN AND BROILER DOOR RELIEF

40.1 The oven and broiler door shall open when a pulling force of 22.6 kg is applied at each door handle in a direction which is normal to the plane of the door when tested by the method given in 40.1.1. 40.1.1 The oven thermostat sha,ll be set at its 26�C setting and the oven shall be operated at normal test pressure for a period of 30 minutes before applymg the test outlined below:
In the case of separate broilers the gas shall be ignited at the broiler burner and the broiler operated at normal test pressure for a period of 30 minutes. A weight of 22.6 kg shall be attached to a point adjacent to the oven or broiler door handle by means of a wire which extends over a pulley, the direction of pull being perpendicu1a.r to the plane of the door. The door shall open easily when the load is applied without jar. As an alternative, test load may be applied by means of a spring scale, held horizontally and attached to the door. When the handle is of such a nature that the application of the load on it will not tend to disengage the door latching mechanism, the wire or spring scale may be attached to the handle. This test shall also be applied with the oven and broiler at room temperature. SECTION 3 GENERAL

METHOD A-l. PROCEDURE

A
HOOD

OF TEST FOR DRAFT

A-l.1 The inlet of a vertical or horizontal-to-vertical type draft hood ;hall be attached in its normal operating position to a fixed Auc pipe. In the case of horizontal-to-vertical type hoods, this attachment shall be secured by means' of 5, mm bolts, one in the upper and one in the lower part of the joint. A vertical compression load equal to 0.89 kg/cm of nominal outlet diamctcr shall he applied without impact to the outlet of the hood.
A-l.2 The inlet of a horizontal or vertical-to-horizontal type draft hood shall be attached in its normal operating position to a fixed flue pip<: 1,). 5 mm bolts. For horizontal type draft hoods, one bolt shall be placed irl the upper and one in the lower part of the joint. For vertical-to-horizontal type draft hoods, the bolts shall be placed through the inlet joint parallcl to the other directly opposite to the outlet connection. .4 `3 m length of 0.50 mm sheet steel flue pipe of suitable diameter shall thctl bc attached in a horizontal position to the outlet connection of the draft hood, the other :nd of the length of pipe being supported at a point not more than 25 mm i-om its extremity. ~1.3 The gas rate to all burners which vent through the draft hood shall 3e adjusted, the gas ignited, and the increased test pressure applied. If top burners are vented through the draft hood, they shall be covered by When a locking device prevents operation of suitable water-filled utensils. separate oven and broiler burners at one time, two tests shall be conducted, one with each burner in operatiorl. A-1.4 After the temperature at the centre of the oven has reached 287'C as indicated by thermocouples the gas supply shall be regulated to maintain this temperature and the test shall be started. The appliance shall be operated for one hour under these conditions. If no distortion of any part of the draft hood is noted at the end of the test period, it shall be considerrd as complying wit6 :his provision.

APPENDIX (Clause35.1)
METHOD FOR MEASUREMENT CAPACITY

C

OF OVEN HEATING

C-l. C-l.1

PROCEDURE

The temperature of the oven shall be measured by an indicating or recording potentiometer and five parallel-connected thermocouples, one located at the centre and the other four equally spaced between the centre and the corners of the oven on the diagonals of a horizontal plane through the centre of the oven. C-1.2 The gas rate shall be adjusted at normal test pressure to within 5 2 percent of the manufacturer's hourly kcal input rating. On ranges equipped with thermostats the dial shall be set at the maximum position. C-l.3 The gas shall be ignited with the oven at room temperature and the time required to reach 260�C noted. The average heating rate shall be computed by means of the following formula and shall not be less than 9.5 degrees/minute. Average heating rate = 260 -Room Observed temperature heating time

OF OVEN HEAT

El.2 The number of cakes baked shall be as specified by the manufacturer but not less than one per 0.093 rn" of rack area (fractional areas are not to be considered). El.3 The cakes shall be baked on a rack in the position nearest the centre The pans shall be symmetrically located and spaced as evenly of the oven. as possible with respect to each other and the sides, front and rear of the oven. El.4 The time required to open the oven door, insert the cake pans, and close the oven door shall not exceed 30 seconds. El.5 The cakes shall be baked for 25 to 30 minutes unless otherwise specified by the manufacturer, removed from oven, cooled to room temperature and measured for reflectance. APPENDIX (Claulse 38.1)
METHOD F-l. PROCEDURE F-l.1 FOR MEASUREMENT TEMPERATURE

F
OF BROILER

Broilers Other Than Open Top Broilers--This test shall be conducted at normal test pressure. Broiler temperatures shall be determined by means of an indicating potentiometer and nine parallel-connected the junctions of which are copper plates iron-constantan thermocouples, 25 mm in diameter and 0.79 mm thick to which the thermocouples wires are silver-soldered 12 mm apart. These discs shall each be located at the centre of the top surface of an asbestos board 37 mm in diameter and 9,5 mm thick. The size of the iron-constantan wires shall be 0.50 mm. The surfaces of the copper discs and asbestos board shall be finished in dull black. F-1.2 The asbestos boards bearing the thermocouples shall be located on rectangular racks in the following manner: one in each corner with its outer edges coinciding with the edges of the rack, one in the centre of the rack and four on the diagonals through the centre of the rack located respectively midway betweep the centre board and each of the four corner boards, When the corner of a rack is cut away to permit access to the broiler pan the board ordinarily placed on this corner shall occupy the same position as it would if the rack were not cut away.
F-1.3 In the case of round broiler racks, the asbestos boards shall be placed as described in F-1.2, on a square which is circumscribed by the outer circumference of the rack, two sides of which are parallel to the front of the unit. F-1.4 The asbestos boards shall be positioned and supported so that the upper surfaces of the copper discs will be a vertical distance of 50 mm below the burner ports, except when the broiler compartment requires a lesser distance, in which case the maximum distance shall be utilized. F-1.4.1 Thermostats, if provided, shall be set at maximum temperature position. With the broiler at room temperature the gas shall be turned on and ignited and both the oven and broiler doors, if any, closed. The average broiler temperature shall be determined and shall have reached 330�C within 30 minutes. F-2. OPEN TOP BROILERS

F-2.1 tures nine which

This test shall be conducted at normal test pressure. Broiler temperashall be determined by means of an indicating potentiometer and paralleI-connected iron-constantan thermocouples, the junctions of are copper plates 25 mm in diameter and 0.80 mm thick, to which 27

IS : 8251- 1976
the thermocouple wires are silver-soldered 12 mm apart. These discs shall be installed flush with the under surface of a 9.5 mm thick asbestos board large enough to cover 75 percent of the grid area. This board shall be shaped so that when centrally positioned on the grid the uncovered area is a space of equal width around the perimeter of the board. The surface of the board shall be divided into 9 sections of equal area and one thermocouple shall be installed at the centre of each section. The size of the ironconstantan wires of the thermocouple junction shall be 0.50 mm. The surfaces of the copper discs and the asbestos board shall he finishrd in dull black. F-2.1.1 With the appliance at room temperature the gas to the broiler burner shall be turned on and ignited. The average broiler temperature shall be determined and shall have reached 330�C within 30 minutes.

APPENDIX (Clause 39.1)
METHOD G-1. PROCEDURE

G
HEAT

FOR MEASUREMENT OF BROILER DISTRIBUTION

G-l.1 This test shall be conduct& at normal test pressure. The broiling area shall bc centrally located with respect to the broiler pan or rack. It shall be markrd off on the broiler pan, or on the broiler rack when no pan is provided, by lines parallel to each edge and in from the edge 6.3 mm the distance to the crntrc. G-l.2 Five individually conncct,ed asbestos disc thermocouples shall be placed in the broiling area, located one in each corner with its outer edges coinciding with the boundary lines and one in the ccntre. The broiler pan then shall be placed in the broiler compartment in its highest position, but with its upper surface no closer to the burner porti than 5 mm. When a broiler door is provided, it shali be closed. The burner shall be placed in operation and temperatures measured with an indicating potentiometer. When the average of the tcmpcratures measured by the 5 thermocouples reaches 315.5"C, the individual temperature readings shall be recorded. The difference bctwecn the maximum and minimum temperature shall not exceed 83�C. 28
